status: experimental; parity passed; no meaningful end-to-end speedup established

methodology.comparison: Latest Q8 Metal + shared masks/direct partial RoPE + DFlash, with fused heads off/on. Four fresh processes per study. Two warmups and ten measured runs per mode, alternating adjacent pair order. Second session reverses recording order and starts fused. Kernel switches outside timing; external synchronized resident seconds include request cleanup and exclude load/file read.
methodology.studies: First study used generic Swift Metal binding. Final study caches immutable Cmlx launch configuration by batch/query length. Same shader in both studies; different binary hashes. Compare modes within each study, not absolute times between studies.
methodology.host: CPU-heavy background workers were present at snapshots. No compiler or GPU profiler from this task ran alongside timing. Neither study establishes an idle-system peak.
methodology.accuracy: Frozen BF16+DFlash token IDs matched on both English fixtures; captured verifier hidden state is compared against the latest Q8 Metal/attention baseline. Not broad multilingual recognition qualification.
methodology.profiles: Diagnostic profiles are debug and synchronized, not release latency. CPU graph-construction timings deliberately exclude GPU eval and use matched eligibility checks. Only end-to-end paired release results support latency claims.
methodology.validation: 42 focused regression tests passed with MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 for independent NumPy FP32 tolerances. Two diagnostic profiles passed; real checkpoint parity and release timings used default TF32. The initial default-TF32 regression run exceeded FP32 tolerance in untouched encoder/draft fixtures; strict mode passed. Release builds, scoped strict SwiftLint and git diff --check passed. Full repository gate deferred by user.
